cards.explanation: The answer is False. I think Job is being sarcastic. Right after that line he says, “But I also have a mind; I am not inferior to you.” (Job 12:3) That's a man saying he can keep up just fine. He is not handing out trophies, friends.

The answer is a laughingstock. Job says, “I am a laughingstock to my friends, though I called on God, and He answered.” (Job 12:4) He says it twice, in fact, and adds that the righteous and upright man is a laughingstock. I think that stings, friends. It's one thing to be laughed at by strangers, and another to be laughed at by your own friends.

The answer is robbers. Job says, “The tents of robbers are safe, and those who provoke God are secure…” (Job 12:6) Think about how that sounds next to what he said about the righteous man. Job is pointing out that robbers' tents are safe while the righteous man is a laughingstock, friends.

The answer is that the hand of the LORD has done this. Job asks, “Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?” (Job 12:9) He sends his friends to the animals, the birds, the earth and the fish for it. The creatures are in on it, and Job is saying his friends should be too, bakers.

The answer is to check them before accepting them. Job asks, “Does not the ear test words as the tongue tastes its food?” (Job 12:11) Your tongue checks before you swallow, and your ear should do the same, friends. I think Job is hinting that his friends' words deserve a taste test.

The answer is God. Job says, “Wisdom and strength belong to God; counsel and understanding are His.” (Job 12:13) He just said wisdom is found with the elderly (Job 12:12), and then he points higher. Long life is a good teacher, friends, but God is where the wisdom comes from.
The answer is True. Job says, “If He holds back the waters, they dry up, and if He releases them, they overwhelm the land.” (Job 12:15) It goes both ways, friends. The waters do what He lets them do.

The answer is False. Job says, “True wisdom and power belong to Him. The deceived and the deceiver are His.” (Job 12:16) Both are named, so saying only the deceived belong to God doesn't match, friends. The verse doesn't leave out the deceiver.

The answer is barefoot. Job says, “He leads counselors away barefoot and makes fools of judges.” (Job 12:17) He says the same about priests in verse 19. I'd feel pretty small walking out of a big room without my shoes, friends.

The answer is that they stagger like drunkards. Job says, “They grope in the darkness without light; He makes them stagger like drunkards.” (Job 12:25) No light, no reason, no map, friends. Just a lot of wandering.

The answer is to speak to the Almighty. Job says, “Yet I desire to speak to the Almighty and argue my case before God.” (Job 13:3) He wants to speak to God Himself, not just to his friends. I think he wants his answer from the One who actually has it, friends.

The answer is remaining silent. Job says, “If only you would remain silent; for that would be your wisdom!” (Job 13:5) He says staying quiet would be their wisdom. It's a sharp line, friends, and I think he means every word.

The answer is True. Job says, “Surely He would rebuke you if you secretly showed partiality.” (Job 13:10) The word secretly is in there, friends. Job is saying that hiding it from people won't hide it from God.

The answer is that they break down easily. Job says, “Your maxims are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.” (Job 13:12) I think the idea is that ashes and clay don't hold up when pressed. Think of a cookie that crumbles the second you pick it up, friends.

The answer is that he'll hope in Him. Job says, “Though He slay me, I will hope in Him.” (Job 13:15) He knows speaking up is a risk, and he still keeps his hope with God. I think that's one of the boldest lines in the whole book, friends.
The answer is True. Job says, “I will still defend my ways to His face.” (Job 13:15) That comes in the same breath as his hope in God. He's holding both at once, friends.

The answer is that he is in the right. Job says, “See now, I have prepared my case; I know that I will be vindicated.” (Job 13:18) Vindicated means cleared, friends. He has prepared his case, and he says he knows how it will come out.

The answer is False. Job says, “Can anyone indict me? If so, I will be silent and die.” (Job 13:19) He doesn't say he'd argue louder. He says he'd be silent. I think that shows how sure he is of his case, friends.
